Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread

Jump to Recipe
by Addison LaBonte September 2, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:56
Instaread

This Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread is everything that goes into a blender, blended smooth, poured into a pan, and baked! No bowls, no mixer, no measuring out spices, and no refined sugar anywhere. This is the loaf to make when you want something genuinely good without any effort!

My Latest Videos

Video Paused

The pumpkin and ripe banana do the sweetening naturally, the rolled oats blend into a soft, tender crumb, and the dark chocolate chips create gooey pockets of chocolate in every slice. It is also one of the most flexible recipes in the collection: maple syrup and honey both work equally well, and if a blender is not available, oat flour and a bowl work just as well.

What is Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread?

Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread is a gluten free quick bread made by blending pumpkin puree, ripe bananas, rolled oats, an egg, maple syrup or honey, and baking soda directly in a blender until smooth, then folding in dark chocolate chips and baking in a loaf pan.

The rolled oats blend into a naturally gluten free flour that holds the loaf together without any refined flour or sugar. It bakes in 35 to 40 minutes and contains no added spices.

Ingredients

  • ½ cup pumpkin purée
  • 1 cup mashed ripe bananas
  • 1 ¾ cups gluten free rolled oats
  • 1 egg
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • ⅓ cup pure maple syrup or honey
  • 1 cup dark chocolate chips

What Each Ingredient Does

Rolled oats, pumpkin, and banana

One and three quarters cups of rolled oats blend directly with everything else into a smooth oat flour that forms the structure of the loaf. Starting with whole oats rather than pre-made oat flour means everything blends in one step. Use certified GF rolled oats to keep the recipe fully gluten free. Oat flour substitutes at one and a half cups if a blender is not available.

Half a cup of pumpkin puree and one cup of mashed ripe banana work together as the primary moisture and natural sweetener. The banana provides concentrated sweetness from ripening and the pumpkin balances it with earthy moisture. Use plain pumpkin puree only, not pumpkin pie filling.

Maple syrup or honey and dark chocolate chips

One third of a cup of maple syrup or honey adds warm natural sweetness alongside the banana. Maple syrup produces a neutral caramel depth; honey produces a more floral sweetness. Both work equally well at the same amount. One cup of dark chocolate chips folds into the batter by hand after blending. Never blend the chips.

A blender breaks them into shavings rather than keeping them whole. Stirring by hand preserves their shape for gooey, defined pockets in every slice. Extra chips pressed into the top before baking make the loaf more visually appealing.

How to make Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread, step by step

First, preheat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Line a bread pan with parchment paper.

Add all of the ingredients except the chocolate chips to a blender. Blend until smooth.

Then, stir in the chocolate chips.

Pour this mixture into the lined pan. Sprinkle more chocolate chips on top if desired.

Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out with only moist crumbs.

Finally, remove from the oven. Cool fully then slice into.

Why This Loaf Bakes Faster Than Most

Most pumpkin banana bread recipes bake for 45 to 60 minutes. This one finishes in 35 to 40 minutes. Blended rolled oats distribute moisture differently than dry flour particles that hydrate during baking. The oats are already fully combined and liquid-incorporated before the pan goes into the oven.

Pumpkin and banana also provide a cohesive, pre-moistened base that sets faster than oil-and-sugar batters. Pull at 35 minutes and check. Moist crumbs on the toothpick is the signal, not a dry-looking loaf.

Tips for the Best Result

Very ripe bananas, no blending the chips, and pull early

Brown-spotted bananas make a noticeably sweeter, more flavorful loaf. In a recipe with no refined sugar and no spices, banana ripeness matters more than in a standard quick bread. Never blend the chips. They shave into invisible slivers instead of gooey pockets.

Always stir by hand after blending. Pull the loaf at moist crumbs. A clean toothpick at 35 to 40 minutes means it has gone too far.

No blender? Use oat flour and mix by hand

Substitute one and a half cups of oat flour for the rolled oats. Mash the bananas and whisk the wet ingredients by hand, then stir in the oat flour and baking soda. The texture will be very similar to the blender version.

Substitutions

Storage

Room temperature: Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days. The pumpkin and banana keep the loaf moist throughout.

Freezer: Slice, wrap each slice tightly, and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature for 20 to 30 minutes before eating.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this loaf gluten free?

Yes, as long as certified gluten free rolled oats are used. Standard rolled oats may be processed in facilities that also handle wheat. Look for the certified GF label if gluten sensitivity is a concern.

Can I use oat flour instead of rolled oats?

Yes. Substitute one and a half cups of oat flour for the rolled oats and mix the batter by hand in a bowl. The blender is not needed when starting with oat flour.

Can I make this vegan?

Yes. Replace the egg with a flax egg (one tablespoon of ground flax mixed with three tablespoons of water, rested for 5 minutes) and use dairy-free dark chocolate chips. Use maple syrup rather than honey to keep it fully vegan.

Why does my loaf look gummy when I cut it warm?

Oat-based loaves need the full cooling time to set their crumb. The oat structure is more delicate than a flour-based crumb when warm and firms completely once cooled. Always wait until the loaf reaches room temperature before slicing.

Can I add spices?

Yes. One teaspoon of cinnamon or half a teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice blend into the batter with the other ingredients. The recipe intentionally omits spices so the pumpkin, banana, and dark chocolate flavors come through cleanly, but the spiced version also tastes excellent.

Get the Recipe: Blender Pumpkin Banana Bread

Moist, soft, and loaded with dark chocolate chips in every slice. The blender does every bit of the work, and the combination of pumpkin and ripe banana produces a naturally sweet, deeply satisfying loaf that tastes indulgent without a single grain of refined sugar.

Ingredients

8 slices
  • ½ cup pumpkin purée
  • 1 cup mashed ripe bananas
  • 1 ¾ cups gluten free rolled oats
  • 1 egg
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, or honey
  • 1 cup dark chocolate chips

Instructions 

  • First, preheat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Line a bread pan with parchment paper.
  • Add all of the ingredients except the chocolate chips to a blender. Blend until smooth.
  • Then, stir in the chocolate chips.
  • Pour this mixture into the lined pan. Sprinkle more chocolate chips on top if desired.
  • Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out with only moist crumbs.
  • Finally, remove from the oven. Cool fully then slice into.

Notes

  • Use brown spotted bananas for the best flavor.
  • You can use oat flour if desired.
  • If you use oat flour, you can mix this by hand if needed.
  • Do not bake too long.
  • Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days at room temperature.
